title: Smoked Mac and Cheese for the Crew
displayTitle: Smoked Mac and Cheese for the Crew
seoTitle: Smoked Mac and Cheese for the Crew | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: The side that turns brisket night into a full spread
subtitle: Creamy three-cheese bake with a light smoke kiss for ten
description: Adapted from classic smoked mac and cheese tradition (Hey Grill Hey, Traeger): elbow pasta bakes in a creamy three-cheese sauce, then rides the smoker at 275°F for 30 minutes for subtle smoke and a golden top.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Smoked Mac and Cheese for the Crew in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch vegetarian. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Par-cook pasta
steps.instruction: Boil macaroni in salted water 2 minutes shy of package directions. Drain well. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build cheese sauce
steps.instruction: Melt butter, whisk in flour 1 minute. Whisk in milk and cream until smooth. Simmer until thick, then melt in cheddar, Gruyère, and gouda. Season with salt, pepper, and paprika. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Combine and pan
steps.instruction: Fold pasta into cheese sauce. Transfer to buttered foil pans. Top with panko mixed with 2 tbsp melted butter. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Smoke at 275°F
steps.instruction: Smoke uncovered at 275°F 30 minutes until top is golden and internal temp reaches 165°F in the center. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest and hold
steps.instruction: Rest 10 minutes. Cover with foil and hold at 170°F until service. Stir edges into center if a skin forms. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Tonight's board
steps.instruction: Mac in foil pans with serving spoons. Pair with any smoked meat on the line. Target 165°F for any egg-based components at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F for any egg-based components. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Reheat covered at 325°F with splash of milk until 165°F. Top with hot sauce for shift lunch. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Undercook pasta—it finishes in the sauce and smoke.
Smoked gouda doubles the smoke note without extra pit time.
165°F in the center means safe hold temp for the crew line.
tonightSpread: Smoked mac in foil pans with serving spoons.
Extra cracked pepper at the table.
leftovers: Fried mac bites coated in panko for next shift.
Stir in pulled pork for a one-pan second day.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Mac is the side crews fight over. Smoker time adds depth without overpowering, and it holds covered at 170°F for 45 minutes.
mealPrepNotes: Build sauce and par-cook pasta ahead. Assemble in foil pans. Smoke 30 minutes, then hold covered at 170°F. Stir before service if top dries.
